title: Variables and types
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to store values in variables, choose good names, and tell the difference between int, float, str and bool.

sections.title: What is a variable?
sections.text: A variable is a name that holds a value, like a labelled box. age = 12 puts the value 12 into a box called age. In Python, = means "store this value", not "is equal to" like in maths.

sections.title: Using and changing a variable
sections.text: Once a variable has a value, you can use its name instead of the value: print(age) shows 12. If you write age = 13 later, the old value is replaced by the new one.

sections.title: Good names
sections.text: Names can use letters, numbers and the underscore _, but they cannot start with a number or contain spaces. Capital letters matter, so Score and score are two different names. Pick names that say what the value is, like total_points instead of x.

sections.title: Four basic types
sections.text: Every value has a type. Whole numbers like 12 are int. Numbers with a decimal point like 1.5 are float. Text in quotes like "Ada" is str (a string). True and False are bool, and they always start with a capital letter. type(value) tells you the type.

examples.title: Example 1: Store and change a value
examples.code:
name = "Ada"
age = 12
print(name)
print(age)
age = 13
print(age)

misconception.1: = stores a new value. It does not add to the old one.

check_questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT allowed as a variable name?
check_questions.explanation: A variable name cannot start with a number.

misconception.1: Numbers are allowed as long as they are not first.
misconception.3: Capital letters are allowed. Score is just a different name from score.

check_questions.explanation: "7" is in quotes, so it is a string, even though it looks like a number.

misconception.0: The quotes make it text, not a whole number.
misconception.2: A float has a decimal point and no quotes.
misconception.3: type() tells you the type, not the value.

try_it.title: Try It Yourself
try_it.instructions: Change the values so they describe you, then run the code. Add a line that prints the type of likes_python.

age = 12
height = 1.5
